notes.2: This question involved calculating distance travelled from the area under a speed/time graph. A significant number of candidates forgot to halve the product of final speed and time.
notes.5: The topic here was extension/load graphs. Many candidates did not realise the significance of the graph starting at the origin, meaning that the vertical axis represented extension rather than measured length. �PAGE�6
notes.16: This question tested understanding of the process of evaporation, and it was generally well answered. However, the popularity of distractor C showed that, although there was awareness that the remaining liquid would cool, the link between this and the lowering of the average energy of its molecules was less widely known.
notes.17: A significant number of candidates gave answers which implied that the pressure of the air in the pump could increase at constant temperature without its volume decreasing.
notes.18: Most responses were correct to this question on sound and hearing, but many candidates opted for C, frequency too high. Candidates should know that the amplitude of a sound wave must also be large enough for the sound to be heard.
notes.20: Most candidates knew the correct order for the electromagnetic spectrum, although a significant proportion chose D, which showed the electromagnetic radiations in order of decreasing frequency.
notes.22: A significant number of candidates chose option D, which showed a mirror facing towards scout Q. This would not be suitable as it would not reflect the ray in the required direction.
notes.31: Most responses were correct to this question on fuses. Some candidates realised that the fuse should be in series with the appliance, but did not know that it should be on the live side.
notes.33: Although the majority of candidates answered this question correctly, a significant minority seemed unaware of this standard method of demagnetisation.
notes.35: Although this question was simple recall, it was not well answered. Option C, the field around a straight wire, was the most popular answer. �PAGE�7
